newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS SEEN INCHING UP ON BARGAIN-HUNTING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS SEEN INCHING UP ON BARGAIN-HUNTING.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen higher on mild bargain-hunting
--Peso likely firm on stable long bond, auction hopes
Dealers saw stocks opening with moderate upside potential on Tuesday on bargain-hunting amid market caution ahead of U.S. inflation data.
"Monday's recovery was encouraging and long bond yields have eased, so we expect some buying, but the big money is waiting for U.S. inflation data," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed resistance at 5,080 points on the IPC index, up from Monday's close of 5,043.65 points.

Traders expected the peso to open firm as pressure had eased from the 30-year Treasury bond, up 8/32 to yield 6.62 percent, and on forecast hikes in domestic interest rates at the central bank auction later in the day.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.7775/7.7875 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.7800/7.7850 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.8010/7.8070.
A firm peso and stable long bond yields were seen anchoring overnight rates on Cetes and holding them close to Monday's close of 19.20 percent.
